b094his: If your cortisol is normal or low, low ATP signaling in the brain might be what's behind your anxiety or depression. Recent neuroscience (Tian-Ming Gao, et al, 2025) has shown in male mice that anxiety and depression are a result of reduced hippocampal astrocyte ATP release. So I'd trial 20mg of PQQ in the morning to boost ATP, with ketones, which your neurons can still burn for energy when they're struggling to burn sugar. In Calabrese, et al (2024), three adults on a ketogenic diet all went into full remission of depression and anxiety within a few months. That's only three people, but it's part of much broader research.
b098-100: Strategy B, the "Resilience Mode", is a keto diet. Carbs stay under 20g/day so the liver makes the ketones itself. Fat becomes your fuel, so eat it until you're full. Don't rely on lean protein like chicken breast alone, because your body turns the extra protein into sugar through gluconeogenesis, and that keeps you out of ketosis. You must pick one of two ketone strategies, because each one needs different electrolytes later. Strategy A, the "Crisis Mode", is for clearing the fog fast. It means a standard low-sugar diet, with your ketones drunk as BHB (beta-hydroxybutyrate) salts.

Strategy B, the "Resilience Mode", is a keto diet. Carbs stay under 20g/day so the liver makes the ketones itself. Fat becomes your fuel, so eat it until you're full. Don't rely on lean protein like chicken breast alone, because your body turns the extra protein into sugar through gluconeogenesis, and that keeps you out of ketosis. To avoid the side effects of switching over, refer to my Keto Adaptation Guide.
